title: Questions and negation
seoTitle: Turkish questions and negation: mi and değil
intro: This unit turns statements into negatives and questions. You'll meet *değil* (not), the question particle `mI`, the question words, the usual ways to answer, and the little word *dA* (too, also). With them you can already hold a short conversation: *Yorgun musun?* (Are you tired?) *Hayır, yorgun değilim. Sen?* (No, I'm not. You?)

blocks.text: To say that someone or something is **not** something, put *değil* (not) after the noun or adjective. *Değil* is a separate word, and the personal ending of **to be** moves onto it: *öğrenciyim* (I am a student) → *öğrenci değilim* (I am not a student).

rows.en: he or she is not a student
you are not a student (polite), you are not students

blocks.text: Because the endings sit on *değil*, they never change with the word before it. The last vowel of *değil* is always i, so you get *-im*, *-sin*, *-iz*, *-siniz* and *-ler* every time: *yorgun değilim*, *hasta değilim*, *Türk değilim*. And since *değil* ends in a consonant, there is never a buffer letter.

blocks.text: **He, she, it** has no ending, as in the positive: *Ali evli değil* (Ali is not married). In formal writing you'll see *değildir*. For **they**, *değiller* is the full form, but *değil* alone is common when *onlar* is in the sentence: *Onlar öğretmen değil*.

Keep the ending off the noun: *öğrenci değilim*, never *öğrenciyim değil*. *Değil* negates nouns and adjectives only. Verbs have a negative suffix of their own ([unit 6](gp-present-continuous-negative)), and **there isn't** is *yok* ([unit 5](gp-var-yok)).

To ask a yes-no question, put the question particle `mI` after the word you are asking about. It is written as a separate word, yet it follows four-way harmony with the word before it, just like a suffix: *mı*, *mi*, *mu* or *mü*.

blocks.label: The question particle
lines: last vowel a, ı  →  mı    hazır mı?
last vowel e, i  →  mi    evli mi?
last vowel o, u  →  mu    yorgun mu?
last vowel ö, ü  →  mü    Türk mü?

blocks.text: The personal ending of **to be** goes on the particle, not on the word: *Yorgun musun?* (Are you tired?). Since the particle ends in a vowel, the buffer *y* appears before `-Im` and `-Iz`: *miyim*, *miyiz*.

rows.en: is he or she a student
are you a student (polite), are you students

blocks.text: **They** is the exception: `-lAr` stays on the word, and the particle follows it in harmony with *-lar* or *-ler*: *öğrenciler mi?*, *yorgunlar mı?* With *onlar* in the sentence you can leave `-lAr` out: *Onlar yorgun mu?*
For a negative question, the particle follows *değil*: *Yorgun değil misin?* (Aren't you tired?). Here is one adjective in all three forms:

**Focus.** `mI` follows the word that carries the question, so moving it changes what you ask. At the end, it asks about the whole statement. After another word, it puts that word in focus, the way stressing a word does in English.

items.en: Is it Ayşe who's the doctor?
items.note: you thought it was someone else
the ending stays on the predicate when `mI` moves forward

blocks.text: **Stress.** The particle itself is never stressed. The syllable just before it is, and the voice rises: *yorGUN musun?*, *öğrenCİ misin?*
Write the particle as a separate word, even though it sounds like part of the word before it. Its vowel copies that word, not the ending that follows: *Türk müsün?*, *evli misiniz?*

Meaning
Example
rows: *Kaç kişisiniz?* How many of you are there?

blocks.text: A question word already makes the sentence a question, so it never takes `mI`: *Bu kim?* (Who is this?) is complete as it is.

The question word stands where the answer will go, usually just before the end of the sentence: *Öğretmen kim?* (Who is the teacher?), *Öğretmen Ayşe Hanım* (The teacher is Ayşe Hanım). Like any noun or adjective, it can carry the ending of **to be**: *Sen kimsin?* (Who are you?), *Nasılsınız?* (How are you?).

*Hangi* always comes with a noun: *Hangi çanta yeni?* (Which bag is new?). *Kaç* is followed by a noun in the singular: *Kaç kişi?* (How many people?), a rule you'll meet again with numbers in [unit 11](gp-numbers-singular).

There are three words for **why**. *Neden* is the everyday one, *niçin* sounds a little more formal, and *niye* more casual. The answer often starts with *çünkü* (because): *Neden üzgünsün?* (Why are you sad?) *Çünkü yorgunum* (Because I'm tired).

items.en: What is the new teacher like?

blocks.text: *Ne* is **what** and *neden* is **why**: *Bu ne?* (What is this?), *Neden?* (Why?). And no `mI` after a question word: *Sen kimsin?*, with the ending on *kim*.
*Ne?* on its own sounds abrupt. To ask someone to repeat, say *Efendim?* ([unit 1](a1-u01)).
*Evet* is **yes** and *hayır* is **no**. Turkish speakers usually add the predicate to them, or simply answer with the predicate alone.

**Tags.** *Değil mi?* turns a statement into a request for confirmation, like **isn't it?** or **right?** It never changes: *Sen Kanadalısın, değil mi?* (You're Canadian, aren't you?), *Bu doğru, değil mi?* (This is true, isn't it?).
*Değil mi?* works like French “n'est-ce pas ?” or a questioning “non ?”. Unlike English **isn't it?** or **aren't you?**, it never changes with the person.
**Negative questions.** To *Yorgun değil misin?* (Aren't you tired?), the clearest answer is the form itself: *Yorgunum* (yes, I am) or *Değilim* (no, I'm not).

items.en: Are you a doctor? Yes, I am.
Is Ali married? No, he isn't.

blocks.text: *Tabii* (of course) is spelled with two i's. *Tabi*, with one, is a different word.
*dA* means **too** or **also**. It is a separate word, placed right after the word it adds, and it follows two-way harmony: *de* after e, i, ö, ü, and *da* after a, ı, o, u.
In a negative sentence, *dA* means **either**: *Ben de yorgun değilim* (I'm not tired either).

items.note: the last line of a Nasreddin Hoca story: see the [interlude](a1-u04-culture)

blocks.text: Unlike the suffixes that start with D, *dA* never turns into *ta*: *Murat da*, *kitap da*. And always write it apart: *ben de* (me too) is not *bende*, which means **on me** or **I've got it** ([unit 5](gp-pronoun-n)).
*Ben de* also answers a greeting or a wish: *Memnun oldum* (Nice to meet you). *Ben de* (Me too).

summary: *Değil* negates nouns and adjectives and carries the personal ending: *yorgun değilim*, *öğrenci değilsin*.
The question particle `mI` is a separate word in four-way harmony: *hazır mı*, *evli mi*, *yorgun mu*, *Türk mü*.
The personal ending goes on `mI`: *yorgun musun?*, *öğrenci miyim?* **They** keeps `-lAr` on the word: *öğrenciler mi?*
`mI` follows the word in focus, and the syllable before it is stressed.
Question words (*kim, ne, nasıl, kaç, hangi, neden, niçin, niye*) never take `mI`.
Answer with *evet* or *hayır*, or simply with the predicate: *Yorgunum.*, *Değilim.* The tag *değil mi?* never changes.
*dA* (too, also; either) is written apart, in two-way harmony, and never turns into *ta*: *ben de*, *Murat da*, *kitap da*.
